note: Phase 6 gate G4 - capacity sweep, single-threaded sim (no Parallel.For yet; that is Phase 8). Method: tools/capacity_sweep.py spawns N cars evenly on the fig8 loop of the `basic` map (rolling start 50 km/h, throttle held), waits 8 s warmup, then measures pace = sim-time advanced / wall-time over a >=25 s sim window. pace >= 0.97 counts as real-time 60 Hz. Both hosts measured with the identical script (same /state polling overhead).
observations: C# holds exact real time up to ~170 cars (pace 0.992), i.e. ~1.9x the Python ceiling (~90).
Per-car speedup is ~2x and roughly constant from 160 to 576 cars.

Pace falls SUPER-linearly with N on both hosts (e.g. C# 200->800: 0.865 -> 0.217): some loop component grows faster than O(N). Candidates for Phase 8 analysis: per-frame UpdateState allocates N dicts (GC pressure), IsOnRoad runs twice per car per frame, spatial-hash rebuild per substep.

Part of the high-N overhead is /state JSON serialization polled every 250 ms by the measurement client - this goes away in the Phase 7 Godot integration (in-process snapshot read), so the embedded ceiling should be at or above these numbers.
